record.paper_title: Pole solutions in the case of problems of flame front propagation and Saffman-Teylor "finger" formation without surface tension: open problems and possible ways of their solutions
record.context_brief: Gaussian-noise saturation-point study for cylindrical flames
record.original_question: In numerical simulations of cylindrical flame-front propagation, does adding explicit Gaussian noise produce a flame-front velocity saturation point, and how does the position or behavior of that saturation point depend on the Gaussian-noise amplitude when extrapolated toward small numerical noise?

evidence.quote: Introduction obvious Gaussian noise results to appearance of a point of saturation and its removal from the origin of coordinates with decreasing of noise amplitude, allowing extrapolating results on small numerical noise. ( Fig. 2.6 in [7]) Hence, introducing of Gaussian noise in numerical calculation also for a cylindrical case can again results to appearance of a saturation point and will allow to investigate its behavior as function of noise amplitude by extrapolating results on small numerical noise. The Inquisitive Reader loved by me is invited again to make it and to publish the received interesting results.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Sivashinsky equation governing the dynamics of an outward-propagating (cylindrical/radial) premixed flame front in two dimensions. Let the front be described by a single-valued function whose evolution is given by the (Michelson–)Sivashinsky equation supplemented with an additive Gaussian white-noise forcing term of amplitude ε > 0:

  ∂_t Φ = (1/2)(∂_x Φ)^2 + ν ∂_x^2 Φ + I[Φ] + ε η(x,t),

where I[Φ] denotes the singular (Landau–Darrieus) linear integral operator with symbol |k|, the geometry is cylindrical (radially outward propagating front of growing radius R(t)), and η is zero-mean Gaussian white noise with unit variance.

Perform numerical simulations of this system and answer the following:

(a) Does the mean propagation velocity V(t) of the cylindrical flame front, computed in the presence of explicit Gaussian noise of amplitude ε, exhibit a finite saturation point — i.e., a time t_sat(ε) (or equivalently a radius R_sat(ε)) at which V transitions from systematic growth/acceleration to an approximately steady (saturated) behaviour?

(b) If such a saturation point exists, determine how its location t_sat(ε) (or R_sat(ε)) and the saturated velocity V_sat(ε) depend on the noise amplitude ε. In particular, characterize the scaling/behaviour of these quantities as ε → 0, and determine whether the extrapolation ε → 0 yields a well-defined limiting saturation behaviour distinct from that produced by intrinsic numerical roundoff noise alone.
artifact.status_search_result: The analogous question for planar and outward-propagating (cylindrical) Sivashinsky fronts with explicit Gaussian forcing has been investigated numerically and analytically: scaling laws for velocity/acceleration versus system size and noise amplitude have been obtained, and in radial geometry external noise is reported as crucial and capable of producing accelerated fronts via the appearance of new poles. While saturation phenomena and noise-amplitude dependence have been documented for related setups (planar, channel, and outward-propagating cases), a complete, quantitative characterization of the saturation point as a function of ε with controlled ε → 0 extrapolation in the cylindrical geometry does not appear to be fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Noise influence on pole solutions of the Sivashinsky equation for planar and outward propagating flames
status_evidence.snippet: Dynamics of planar and outward propagating cylindrical flames is studied in terms of exact solutions of the Sivashinsky equation with a random force term... modification of pole solutions taking into account appearance of new poles captures features typical for hydrodynamically unstable flames.
status_evidence.claim: The cylindrical/outward-propagating case with Gaussian noise has been partially analysed and scaling features described.

status_evidence.title: Random noise and pole dynamics in unstable front propagation
status_evidence.snippet: Simulations lead to scaling laws for the velocity and acceleration of the front as a function of the system size and the level of noise.
status_evidence.claim: Scaling of velocity with noise amplitude is established for related geometries.

status_evidence.title: General View of Pole Solutions in Flame Front Propagation
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of pole-decomposition solutions of Sivashinsky equation for planar and cylindrical flames including the role of noise.
status_evidence.claim: Survey treats the cylindrical case but leaves a complete saturation-point characterization unresolved.
